jobs.description:
Pinnacle, part of The Pennant Group family, is currently seeking entrepreneurial leaders with proven results in building and leading exceptional teams and has a passion for the senior living industry. Join us in making an impact and shaping the future of senior care!

About the Opportunity:

The CEO-in-Training (CIT) Program
is designed to prepare outstanding leaders for an opportunity to run one of our assisted living, independent living, or memory care communities. This salaried, full-time training program
typically lasts 3–6 months, depending on your background and experience. CITs may advance to lead one of our thriving communities or future acquisition, with continued mentorship and operational support from experienced partners.

As a CIT, you will gain hands-on practical experience in operations, clinical care, and business management under the guidance of an experienced Executive Director/CEO. The program offers mentorship, cross-functional training, and real responsibility in a dynamic environment. You’ll learn to drive results, cultivate a strong team culture, and develop a deep understanding of the unique business models that power Pennant’s success.

Key Responsibilities:

Engage in immersive, on-the-job training across operational, care, and administrative functions
Shadow department heads and front-line staff to understand the day-to-day rhythm of community life
Take the lead on real-time projects and contribute to meaningful improvements within your host community
Study relevant state regulations and best practices in senior living operations
Align leadership and interpersonal skills with Pinnacle’s core values and mission

Minimum Requirements:

3–5 years of leadership experience in any industry
Proven success in building and leading high-performing teams
Ability to inspire, set vision, and deliver measurable results
Must obtain any required state licensing during their CIT program (varies by state)
Open to relocation based on available opportunities

Bachelor’s degree (MBA, MHA, or related field a plus)
Experience in operations, financial management or business development
Entrepreneurial mindset and a heart for service

As part of the Pennant family—a growing national network with over 180 affiliated locations across 14 states spanning home health, hospice, and senior living—we operate with the independence and flexibility that allow our local leaders to truly make a difference. Pennant Services provides robust clinical, legal, accounting, IT and HR support, enabling our teams to focus on delivering exceptional service and care.

We are guided by the core values that shape Pennant’s unique culture:

jobs.description:
About Juntos Community

Juntos Community helps undocumented immigrants and mixed-status families access upward mobility and build generational wealth. Founded in 2020, the organization has supported thousands of community members through programs centered on protection, opportunity, and economic empowerment.

Juntos Community is undergoing a strategic rightsizing process to strengthen its long-term impact. A central priority is preserving DACAWorks, its flagship program supporting DACA renewals, legal education, clinics, and grantmaking for low-income recipients.

Position Summary

Juntos Community is seeking a strategic, adaptable, and mission-driven Managing Director to guide the organization through this transition while sustaining its commitment to undocumented immigrants and mixed-status families.

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Managing Director will oversee organizational operations, fundraising, financial stability, and DACAWorks. The Managing Director will also help develop Juntos Community’s 2027–2029 operating plan in partnership with the Board and transitioning Founder/CEO.
This is a full-time, hybrid position based in Denver, Colorado, requiring in-office presence at least two days per week, currently Tuesdays and Thursdays.

Key Responsibilities

Organizational Leadership and Governance

• Provide the Board with regular updates on operations, finances, fundraising, and organizational sustainability
• Partner with the Board on budgeting, strategic planning, and long-term organizational direction
• Maintain essential administrative systems, compliance obligations, and financial operations
Fundraising and Revenue Generation
• Lead fundraising efforts, including grant writing and reporting, donor and foundation stewardship, annual campaigns, and Board fundraising
• Help develop a sustainable fundraising and revenue plan for 2027–2029
• Explore fee-for-service opportunities through virtual clinics, trainings, consultations, and DACA renewal support
• Build partnerships and systems that diversify revenue and increase community participation

Program and Staff Oversight

• Supervise and support the DACAWorks Program Manager
• Ensure the continued effectiveness of DACA clinics, renewals, legal education, and grant distribution
• Support staff accountability, morale, and continuity during organizational change
• Identify potential partnerships or program transitions when appropriate
Community and External Relations
• Maintain trust and visibility with undocumented communities and organizational partners
• Represent Juntos Community in funder conversations, community meetings, and select public opportunities
• Protect the organization’s community-centered mission, values, and reputation throughout the transition

Qualifications

• At least three years of nonprofit leadership or senior management experience
• Experience working with a Board of Directors and reporting on finances, fundraising, and strategy
• Demonstrated experience with nonprofit fundraising, grant writing, donor stewardship, and financial management
• Experience supervising staff and maintaining morale during organizational change
• Strong relationship-building and communication skills
• Commitment to serving undocumented immigrants and mixed-status families
• Ability to work independently and balance operational, fundraising, and program responsibilities in a lean organization
• Bilingual English/Spanish skills strongly preferred
• Experience with immigration services, DACA programming, fee-for-service models, or organizational rightsizing is highly valued
• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional or lived experience

Compensation and Benefits

Salary: $80,000–$89,000, depending on experience, guaranteed for the first six months.
Benefits include a generous paid-time-off policy and a $2,000 health stipend during the first six months. Juntos Community does not currently offer comprehensive health insurance or retirement benefits but intends to work toward a broader benefits package following the initial six-month period.

Preferred Start Date
: On or before November 2, 2026

How to Apply

The search is being led by Marisol Solarte-Erlacher and Sonya Ulibarri of Cultura Leadership Consulting. Please submit a résumé and cover letter describing your interest and qualifications to info@culturaleadership.com.
Applications will be reviewed as received until the position is filled. Priority consideration will be given to applications received by 11:59 p.m. on Sunday, August 30.

Chastain Horse Park
is a nonprofit therapeutic horsemanship center located in Atlanta’s historic Chastain Park empowering individuals of all abilities through life-changing relationships with horses. As one of only two urban horse parks remaining in the United States and a Premier Accredited PATH Intl. center, Chastain Horse Park serves children, adults, veterans, seniors, and families through therapeutic riding, equine-assisted services, physical and occupational therapy, and mental health programs. Supported by a herd of more than 25 horses, thousands of volunteer service hours, and a network of healthcare, education, and community partners, Chastain Horse Park delivers measurable physical, cognitive, emotional, and social outcomes for participants.

Chastain Horse Park is seeking an experienced Director of Operations

This role reports to the Executive Director and is responsible for aligning our professional teams around measurable goals, establishing consistent processes and documentation, and driving accountability and collaboration across the organization. We are looking for a leader who can think strategically while managing the day-to-day realities of a complex, multi-use equestrian operation.

Leadership & Team Management : Provide experienced leadership and direction to Chastain Horse Park's programming and operational leaders, including Therapeutic, Boarder, School Programs as well as Barn Management and Facilities.
Establish clear goals, expectations, and accountability across teams
Lead administrative efforts integrating people, programs, facilities, systems, and resources to deliver exceptional experiences for participants, horses, staff, volunteers, and the community.
Lead performance management and professional development efforts
Strengthen organizational leadership capability
Foster a culture of collaboration, ownership, and continuous improvement

Culture and Communication : Create and champion a welcoming, inclusive, and connected Chastain Horse Park community for employees, participants, families, volunteers, boarders, and partners.
Support consistent employee, customer and partner onboarding, communication, and engagement practices
Lead efforts to measure and maintain satisfaction across all constituents including customers, volunteers, partners and other community members
Lead and oversee efforts to measure and maintain program impact data
Promote a culture grounded in respect, trust, service, and shared purpose
Help strengthen a unified "One Chastain Horse Park " experience across all programs

Program & Operational Excellence : Ensure all Chastain Horse Park programs and operations function effectively, efficiently, and in alignment with the organization's mission and strategic priorities.
Provide leadership and oversight of daily operations across all programs and facilities
Establish clear annual goals, KPIs, and operating expectations for each program area.
Ensure effective coordination, communication, and problem-solving across teams
Develop and implement standardized policies, procedures, and operational practices

Safety, Risk Management, and Standards : Ensure a safe, well-managed environment for participants, staff, volunteers, and horses.
Ensure adherence to safety protocols and risk management practices
Ensure programming remains in compliance with PATH Intl Premier Accreditation standards
Promote organization-wide accountability for safety and well-being
Support the highest standards of horse care and operational stewardship

Financial & Strategic Leadership : Partner with the Executive Director to execute organizational priorities and ensure sustainable performance.
Manage operational budgets and resources responsibly
Use performance data and operational insights to support decision-making
Contribute to strategic planning and organizational goal setting
Drive achievement of programmatic, operational, and financial objectives

Qualifications:

Required
Experience leading teams in complex, multi-program service organizations
Proven successful development of leaders and creation of high-performing teams
Strong organizational, communication, and relationship-building skills
Proven ability to manage strategic priorities with effective day-to-day execution
Demonstrated accountability, performance metrics, and operational processes

Preferred
Working understanding of horses and equestrian environments
Experience in a nonprofit or mission-driven organization
Passion for serving individuals with physical, cognitive, and emotional disabilities

Key Competencies
Strategic thinking with strong execution
Ability to thrive in a complex environment
Leadership and accountability
Team development and coaching

Compensation
: Chastain Horse Park offers highly competitive compensation ( commensurate with experience) including company paid health insurance.

Why This Role Matters

At Chastain Horse Park, horses change lives—but it’s people who make that possible. This role ensures that the people, programs, and operations come together in a way that delivers that impact—every day for every participant, team member, volunteer, and of course every horse.

Work directly with ownership and investment partners to shape the long-term direction of the platform.

Have access to meaningful financial backing to pursue an ambitious acquisition strategy.
Have significant influence over strategy, M&A, culture, talent and commercial growth.

A major component of the role will be M&A and founder partnerships. You'll develop and execute the acquisition strategy, identify attractive businesses, establish relationships with owners, understand their objectives and ultimately create partnerships that work for both sides.

Setting and executing the platform's long-term strategic direction.

We're particularly interested in individuals who have built, scaled, acquired or integrated roofing businesses and are now looking for the platform, capital and mandate to take their impact to the next level.

There are plenty of CEO roles where the job is to maintain what already exists. This isn't one of them. The platform has the backing, acquisition strategy and ambition to create something considerably larger.

jobs.description:
The Director of Development will direct the overall strategy and fundraising operation on behalf of Johns Hopkins University and for a smaller development office (DOFF), department, area or division. The Director will play a significant role in department or DOFF operations, which includes serving as a member of its senior administrative team, and providing substantial input into the strategy and management of its philanthropic priorities and stewardship including major gift cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship, annual giving, and constituent engagement and may include oversight of other portfolios such as corporate and foundation giving, alumni relations, stewardship and events. The Director will manage and set goals for a team in support of Johns Hopkins’ ambitious fundraising goals.

The Department of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery currently raises $1M-$2M annually in philanthropic support but is poised for significant growth as it expands its faculty, clinical programs, research enterprise, educational initiatives, and global reach. This role will be responsible for building a proactive and sophisticated fundraising program capable of identifying, cultivating, and securing support from major donors, grateful patients, foundations, alumni, and other philanthropic partners.

The Director of Development will serve as the department’s chief fundraising strategist and build and manage a comprehensive major and principal gifts program. Working in close partnership with Dr. St. John, faculty leaders, grateful patients, alumni, and institutional partners, the Director of Development will develop and execute fundraising strategies that secure critical support for research, education, and patient care, and strategic initiatives.

Founded in 1914, the Johns Hopkins Department of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery has over a century of history in clinical excellence and research innovation. It pioneered American sinus surgery, established the first US temporal bone lab, and is a global leader in cancer care. Today, the department is directed by renowned surgeon and physician-scientist Dr. Maie St. John, MD, PhD, Andelot Professor of Laryngology and Otology.

Specific Duties & Responsibilities

Lead a complex team of professional and support staff, including directing personnel actions such as hiring, performance appraisals, promotions and transfers, and vacations schedules, among others. Direct reports will typically include at least two fundraising professionals, and will include an additional area such as communications, finance or data.
Implement fundraising strategies and priorities for a complex division or department(s). Evaluate and update strategies as needed to meet long- and short-range goals and objectives to ensure the successful completion of individual and cumulative team solicitation and fundraising goals. Oversee the strategy and execution of all stewardship efforts for specific department(s) and/or division(s).
Create and implement strategies for pipeline building through data analytics and outreach.
Oversee, mentor, and motivate team members by assigning tasks, monitoring performance, resolving conflicts and ensuring compliance with JHU policies to achieve organizational goals. Ensure that the team is well-supported to reach its goals and is engaged in activities that support development in various parts of the organization.
Align team activities towards building, strengthening, and sustaining relationships with key stakeholders to advance departmental and organizational priorities.
Cultivate and maintain an active portfolio of major and principal gift level donors and prospects, engage directly in the cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of individuals, foundations, and/or corporations. Individual fundraising goals should consistently be $1M or greater.
Develop and execute personalized cultivation strategies to engage and build relationships with prospects.

The Associate Director of Development is a frontline fundraiser responsible for the qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of major gift prospects. The Associate Director will identify, engage, and solicit donors at all life stages, including prospect research, development of effective solicitation strategies and stewardship of donors throughout the major giving process. The Associate Director will typically maintain a donor portfolio with a focus on gifts of $50,000 or above. The Associate Director may require frequent travel and meetings on and off campus during regular and non-traditional business hours and is expected to operate with high levels of autonomy.

The Associate Director of Development of the Johns Hopkins Heart and Vascular Institute serves as one of two front-line fundraisers and works side-by-side with the Director of Development in the management of private sector fundraising. Their portfolio includes faculty from both divisions who specialize in a wide range of cardiovascular specialties. The role is focused on cultivating mid-level and major gift prospects; upgrading high-end annual donors; identifying new donors through patient education events, crowdfunding campaigns, and large-scale prospecting and solicitation collaborations with the Office of Medical Annual Giving.

This position offers a unique opportunity to gain broad exposure to two unique but interrelated areas of academic medicine. The associate director will be an integral member of a team of three, responsible for raising an average of $7.5 million per year in private support. The HVI and Department of Medicine’s development teams are closely affiliated, as the Division of Cardiology is the largest division within the Department of Medicine.

The Johns Hopkins Heart and Vascular Institute (HVI) consists of the Division of Cardiology in the Department of Medicine and the Division of Cardiac Surgery in the Department of Surgery. The HVI is led by clinical and surgical co-directors who work together to ensure a seamless approach to all adult cardiovascular patient care, research, and teaching. The HVI development office supports fundraising activities for both divisions.

The opportunity:

Confidential CEO Search

Our client is a highly ambitious investment-backed platform with a clear objective: build a best-in-class, national services business through strategic acquisitions, partnerships and organic growth.
With significant capital available to deploy, the business is actively pursuing opportunities to partner with established roofing contractors and entrepreneurial founders across the United States.

The model is deliberately different from traditional private equity. The platform is built around partnering with high-quality roofing businesses, providing the capital, infrastructure, resources and leadership required to accelerate growth, while preserving the entrepreneurial culture, customer relationships and operational strengths that made those businesses successful in the first place.

With an active acquisition strategy and substantial runway for further investment, this is an opportunity for an experienced roofing executive to step into a genuine CEO-level build-and-scale role, rather than simply inherit an established operation. The successful candidate will ultimately be responsible for turning a collection of high-performing roofing businesses into a cohesive, scalable and nationally recognized platform.

What's in it for you:

This is an opportunity to join a well-capitalized platform at a pivotal stage of its growth.

You'll have the opportunity to:
Lead a national acquisition and growth strategy across the US roofing market.
Work directly with ownership and investment partners to shape the long-term direction of the platform.
Build relationships with roofing company founders and owners and become the trusted partner throughout the acquisition process.
Have access to meaningful financial backing to pursue an ambitious acquisition strategy.
Have significant influence over strategy, M&A, culture, talent and commercial growth.
Participate in a compelling long-term incentive and equity structure aligned with the value you create.

The role:

As CEO, you'll take overall responsibility for the growth and performance of the platform, working closely with the investment team and existing operating leadership.

A major component of the role will be M&A and founder partnerships. You'll develop and execute the acquisition strategy, identify attractive businesses, establish relationships with owners, understand their objectives and ultimately create partnerships that work for both sides.

You'll be responsible for:

Setting and executing the platform's long-term strategic direction.
Driving organic revenue and EBITDA growth across the operating companies.
Building a scalable national leadership structure.
Establishing consistent operational and financial disciplines.
Developing sales, recruiting and operational capabilities.
Identifying opportunities for cross-company collaboration and shared infrastructure.
Maintaining a strong acquisition pipeline.
Working with the investment team on capital allocation and future growth initiatives.
Creating a culture that attracts and retains exceptional roofing talent and entrepreneurial leaders.

Who we're looking for:

We're looking for an accomplished roofing industry executive, CEO, President, COO or senior operating leader who understands how to build and scale businesses.

You may already have experience leading a multi-location roofing business, a regional/national roofing group or an acquisition-led platform. Most importantly, you'll understand the roofing industry from the inside and have the credibility to sit across the table from founders and owners.

You'll ideally bring:

Significant leadership experience within commercial roofing
A proven track record of growing revenue and profitability.
Experience leading through acquisitions or integrations
Strong commercial and operational instincts.
Experience managing senior leadership teams across multiple locations.
A strong understanding of the economics and operating dynamics of the roofing industry.

We're particularly interested in individuals who have built, scaled, acquired or integrated roofing businesses and are now looking for the platform, capital and mandate to take their impact to the next level.

There are plenty of CEO roles where the job is to maintain what already exists. This isn't one of them. The platform has the backing, acquisition strategy and ambition to create something considerably larger.

new_jobs.title: Director of Development, Department of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery
new_jobs.description:
The Director of Development will direct the overall strategy and fundraising operation on behalf of Johns Hopkins University and for a smaller development office (DOFF), department, area or division. The Director will play a significant role in department or DOFF operations, which includes serving as a member of its senior administrative team, and providing substantial input into the strategy and management of its philanthropic priorities and stewardship including major gift cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship, annual giving, and constituent engagement and may include oversight of other portfolios such as corporate and foundation giving, alumni relations, stewardship and events. The Director will manage and set goals for a team in support of Johns Hopkins’ ambitious fundraising goals.

The Department of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery currently raises $1M-$2M annually in philanthropic support but is poised for significant growth as it expands its faculty, clinical programs, research enterprise, educational initiatives, and global reach. This role will be responsible for building a proactive and sophisticated fundraising program capable of identifying, cultivating, and securing support from major donors, grateful patients, foundations, alumni, and other philanthropic partners.

The Director of Development will serve as the department’s chief fundraising strategist and build and manage a comprehensive major and principal gifts program. Working in close partnership with Dr. St. John, faculty leaders, grateful patients, alumni, and institutional partners, the Director of Development will develop and execute fundraising strategies that secure critical support for research, education, and patient care, and strategic initiatives.

Founded in 1914, the Johns Hopkins Department of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery has over a century of history in clinical excellence and research innovation. It pioneered American sinus surgery, established the first US temporal bone lab, and is a global leader in cancer care. Today, the department is directed by renowned surgeon and physician-scientist Dr. Maie St. John, MD, PhD, Andelot Professor of Laryngology and Otology.

Specific Duties & Responsibilities

Lead a complex team of professional and support staff, including directing personnel actions such as hiring, performance appraisals, promotions and transfers, and vacations schedules, among others. Direct reports will typically include at least two fundraising professionals, and will include an additional area such as communications, finance or data.
Implement fundraising strategies and priorities for a complex division or department(s). Evaluate and update strategies as needed to meet long- and short-range goals and objectives to ensure the successful completion of individual and cumulative team solicitation and fundraising goals. Oversee the strategy and execution of all stewardship efforts for specific department(s) and/or division(s).
Create and implement strategies for pipeline building through data analytics and outreach.
Oversee, mentor, and motivate team members by assigning tasks, monitoring performance, resolving conflicts and ensuring compliance with JHU policies to achieve organizational goals. Ensure that the team is well-supported to reach its goals and is engaged in activities that support development in various parts of the organization.
Align team activities towards building, strengthening, and sustaining relationships with key stakeholders to advance departmental and organizational priorities.
Cultivate and maintain an active portfolio of major and principal gift level donors and prospects, engage directly in the cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of individuals, foundations, and/or corporations. Individual fundraising goals should consistently be $1M or greater.
Develop and execute personalized cultivation strategies to engage and build relationships with prospects.
Build and maintain strong relationships with faculty and administrative leaders and fundraise to support and execute their vision for the particular unit. Work with the leader to maximize the appeal and giving potential for donors by shaping and refining the philanthropic strategy for the assigned unit. Create strong working relationships with the various divisions and departments across the university.
Develop and maintain a comprehensive understanding of school/divisional/departmental mission, history, teaching, research, and/or clinical programs to effectively communicate funding opportunities. Stay abreast of school/divisional/departmental collaborative partnerships, priorities, and shared goals. Train and debrief internal colleagues on current priorities and cases for support.
Lead the recruitment and management of the department’s volunteers and advisory board, leveraging volunteerism toward giving.
Ensure compliance with all relevant regulations and ethical standards. Advocate and ensure donor intent is honored in funds distribution and utilization. Represent the department(s) and/or division at public events and speaking engagements.
May manage personnel and operating budgets directly or at the direction of a senior leader.
Collaborate with DAR leadership on high-priority, high-visibility tasks.
Other duties as assigned.

In addition to the duties described above, the Director of Development will:

Collaborate directly and autonomously with the Chief Administrator and Chief Financial Officer to advance department-wide strategic priorities and fundraising initiatives, including budget planning, revenue projections, and philanthropic forecasting. Ensure clear, consistent communication and alignment with the Department Chair and Chief Administrator.
Oversee the development team’s operations, including gift processing, donor acknowledgments, and stewardship, ensuring accuracy, efficiency, and full compliance with donor intent and organizational standards.
Partner effectively and transparently with development colleagues across JHM, particularly within the National Capital Region-affiliated hospitals and practices, to advanced shared fundraising priorities, support the needs of faculty and patient care teams, and ensure philanthropic opportunities are aligned with both departmental objectives and the strategic goals of partner institutions.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree.
Seven years professional level related experience, including one year of supervisory/management experience.
Additional education may substitute for required experience and additional related experience may substitute for required education beyond a high school diploma/graduation equivalent, to the extent permitted by the JHU equivalency formula.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree (Master’s or JD).
Higher education and/or academic medical center fundraising experience
Proven solicitation success at the major gift ($100k+) level. Strong preference for success at the seven-figure level.
Supervisory experience of other frontline fundraisers, including mentorship of early career staff
Experience setting vision and multi-lateral goals for a team
Experience leading large-scale or cross functional initiatives or projects
Possess leadership characteristics in the following areas:
Build effective networks and working relationships
Consistently manage, encourage, and provide feedback to others to strengthen skills and fulfill job requirements
Show a commitment to building consensus and collaboration while holding self and others accountable
Lead by example in adaptability and empathy
Act with authenticity, transparency
Navigate the organization with purpose, focused on vision, mission and strategy.

Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook).
Familiarity working in a CRM system.

new_jobs.description:
The Associate Director of Development is a frontline fundraiser responsible for the qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of major gift prospects. The Associate Director will identify, engage, and solicit donors at all life stages, including prospect research, development of effective solicitation strategies and stewardship of donors throughout the major giving process. The Associate Director will typically maintain a donor portfolio with a focus on gifts of $50,000 or above. The Associate Director may require frequent travel and meetings on and off campus during regular and non-traditional business hours and is expected to operate with high levels of autonomy.

The Associate Director of Development of the Johns Hopkins Heart and Vascular Institute serves as one of two front-line fundraisers and works side-by-side with the Director of Development in the management of private sector fundraising. Their portfolio includes faculty from both divisions who specialize in a wide range of cardiovascular specialties. The role is focused on cultivating mid-level and major gift prospects; upgrading high-end annual donors; identifying new donors through patient education events, crowdfunding campaigns, and large-scale prospecting and solicitation collaborations with the Office of Medical Annual Giving.

This position offers a unique opportunity to gain broad exposure to two unique but interrelated areas of academic medicine. The associate director will be an integral member of a team of three, responsible for raising an average of $7.5 million per year in private support. The HVI and Department of Medicine’s development teams are closely affiliated, as the Division of Cardiology is the largest division within the Department of Medicine.

The Johns Hopkins Heart and Vascular Institute (HVI) consists of the Division of Cardiology in the Department of Medicine and the Division of Cardiac Surgery in the Department of Surgery. The HVI is led by clinical and surgical co-directors who work together to ensure a seamless approach to all adult cardiovascular patient care, research, and teaching. The HVI development office supports fundraising activities for both divisions.

Specific Duties & Responsibilities

Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward a prospect pool for new and existing annual and major gifts.
Design and implement development strategies to build a portfolio, involving relevant colleagues where necessary.
Determine annual work plan goals in consultation with departmental/divisional development leadership.
Track fundraising activity in the CRM.
Plan and execute solicitation strategies leading to annual and major gifts.
Prepare proposals, solicitation letters, gift agreements, and other development materials for prospects and donors that articulate Johns Hopkins University’s needs, values, and ambitions.
Develop and maintain comprehensive understanding of department or division mission, history, teaching, research, and/or clinical programs to effectively communicate funding opportunities. Learn and actively refresh knowledge of school/divisional/departmental collaborative partnerships, priorities, and shared goals.
Proactively communicate with major prospects and donors about specific ways to give, both current and deferred, to maximize gift and tax benefits.
Complete in-person and virtual donor visits each fiscal year. Goals for visits and other KPIs will be set by school/division/business unit leadership
Develop and participate in implementing annual stewardship plans for donors.
Develop and maintain strong, trust-based partnerships with colleagues across the institution.
Work with faculty and institutional leaders to engage them as fundraising partners in identifying, cultivating, and soliciting prospective donors. Staff, train, and successfully guide internal stakeholders through the development process.
Partner with team members on the planning and executions of development related activities for the department including professorship dedications, lectureships, and other stewardship events.
Participate and engage in team-wide activities, meetings, events, and knowledge-sharing.
Represent school/division on committees and at institution-wide programming where appropriate.
Analyze data at a high level, identify prospects, demonstrate activity, and track progress toward work plan goals.
Participate in special projects, programs, initiatives as assigned.
Other duties as assigned.

In addition to the duties described above, the Associate Director will:

Staff 15-20 core faculty members and additional faculty as needed to train and advise them on best practices for growing their donor portfolios. Solicit and secure contributions on their behalf.
Act as a primary development point of contact for coordination of development involvement and solicitation strategies connected to HVI patient education events, donor-driven fundraising events, online marketing platforms such as Thankview and Constant Contact, and HVI Annual giving solicitations managed by the Office of Medical Annual Giving.
Develop a comprehensive understanding of the research, teaching, and patient care activity of the Johns Hopkins Medicine’s Divisions of Cardiology and Cardiac Surgery and their integrated roles within the Departments of Medicine and Surgery.
Assist Director of Development in coordination and implementation of Cardiovascular Advisory Board activity and volunteer engagement opportunities.
Provide expertise in data mining and analysis and report generation for the identification and cultivation of new HVI donor prospects.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree.
Three years of related experience, with one year of professional experience.
Additional education may substitute for required experience and additional related experience may substitute for required education beyond a high school diploma/graduation equivalent, to the extent permitted by the JHU equivalency formula.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced degree (Master's or JD)
Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook).
Proficiency in data mining, reporting, analysis, and application
A high degree of emotional intelligence; this individual must navigate conversations with patients and family members who are often dealing with serious medical issues and events
Aptitude for understanding and translating medical terminology and research into lay language.
Experience with planned and estate gifts
Crowdfunding experience
Ability to attend periodic evening and weekend work or early arrival when staffing HVI development and patient education events.
